title: Quantization regression autopsy + lightweight smoke-suite and delta-budgeting for rollout gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Model/config rollouts that change quantization profiles (AWQ/GPTQ, int8/int4, mixed precision) occasionally introduce subtle quality regressions that escape coarse unit tests. We need a fast, reproducible post-change analysis (autopsy) and a lightweight smoke-suite to run on PRs/nightly to catch regressions early. Goal: define automated evals, clear gating thresholds (delta-budgeting), and a repeatable investigation playbook so rollouts can be validated with tight, explainable SLOs for quality vs savings.
proposal:
1) Implement a two-tier eval system: a) Smoke-suite: O(100-500) short fast prompts across representative cohorts to run on PRs and preflight for deploys; b) Autopsy-suite: deeper cohort-driven comparative runs (1k-5k prompts) that produce explainable diffs, metric heatmaps, and suggested mitigations (e.g., different quant profile, restore int8->float fallback on heavy-loss cohorts).

2) Delta-budgeting: compute a single weighted delta score across metrics (semantic similarity, task accuracy, generation divergence, hallucination proxy) with budgeted allowable delta per rollout type (canary vs full).

3) Integrations: a) GitHub PR check to fail if smoke-suite exceeds per-metric thresholds; b) Nightly full autopsy runs and a dashboard sliceable by cohort, model variant, quant profile; c) Rollout gate policy in deployment orchestration: automatic rollback on high-severity breaches or manual review for borderline cases.

4) Tooling: a common harness library that can run AWQ/GPTQ profiles reproducibly, capture logits/KV-caches for debugging, and produce per-example diffs and minimal reproduction bundles for triage.
acceptance_criteria: Smoke-suite runs as a GitHub PR check and finishes within PR CI budget (~6 minutes max) on dedicated infra
Autopsy-suite runs nightly and produces a digestible report and heatmaps in the dashboard for any profiles changed
Delta-budgeting score computed and stored for each run; rollout gate rules consult this score to allow/deny canary expansion
Playbook documented with reproducible steps to run per-example autopsies, including commands to re-run with alternate quant profiles
One documented incident-level test where an AWQ-int4 regression was detected by the smoke-suite and a rollback flow was exercised (can be simulated)
tasks: Design smoke-suite prompt set: 12 cohorts (conversational, summarization, code-gen short, code-gen long, QA, instruction-following, math, embeddings similarity, translation, multi-turn state, retrieval + generation, edge-case hallucination prompts)
Implement harness support for AWQ and GPTQ profile loading with seedable compilation artifacts
Add metric collectors: embedding cosine, task-specific accuracy/EM/F1 where applicable, token-level edit-distance, response-length distribution, latency and token cost deltas
Implement delta-budgeting aggregator with weight config per cohort and per-metric default weights
Create PR check GitHub action that runs smoke-suite and posts results as a check run with annotations for failed prompts
Build autopsy report generator (csv + HTML heatmap) and wire to Console dashboard storage
Define rollout gate policies (thresholds for canary vs full rollout) and integrate with deployment orchestration
Write runbook for triage and create sample reproduction bundle for common failure modes
notes: Initial baseline run (2025-03-05) executed against model v3.1 float32 and AWQ-int4 profile. Observed cohort-level regression in 'code-gen long' where pass@1 dropped ~6% and embedding cosine decreased 0.018 vs float baseline. Latency decreased by 38% and cost per token improved by ~2.7x. Next step is to run mixed-precision (some layers kept in fp16) and tuned AWQ params to see if we can regain accuracy within delta-budget.
investigation_playbook: 1) Reproduce locally with sample reproduction bundle from autopsy report. 2) Re-run failure cohort with: float32 baseline, AWQ-int8, AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4, mixed-precision profile. 3) Collect per-token logit diffs and top-k prediction shifts; produce BLEU/EM changes for task-specific prompts. 4) If degradation concentrated in long-context, test larger KV-cache and alternate chunking; if hallucination rate increases, run hallucination classifier on outputs. 5) If a quant profile shows consistent regression, propose a narrower rollout (canary only) or adjust profile to keep problematic layers in higher precision. 6) Document findings and recommended gate action (rollback, proceed with narrow canary, or ship with mitigation).
rolling_strategy: Canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with metric sampling at each step. Canary expands if delta-budget score < low-severity threshold; stops and alerts if score > high-severity threshold. Manual approval required for mid-severity breaches.
observability_plan: Add per-run time-series: weighted-delta-score, per-cohort worst-metric, p95 latency delta, cost-per-token delta. Create alerting: >0.01 absolute embedding cosine drop for high-value cohorts OR >5% absolute accuracy drop triggers PagerDuty; borderline breaches create SRE/Oncall Slack notification and PM/Eng review ticket.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Risk: smoke-suite false positives on brittle prompts; mitigate by cohort weighting and using ensemble of metrics.
- Tradeoff: stricter gating reduces rollout velocity and potential cost savings; delta-budgeting allows targeted exceptions per rollout type.
- Complexity: supporting AWQ/GPTQ cast variants increases maintenance; start with minimal supported profiles and expand.
